Vanessa, can I ask your advice? I have two job offers, and I can't make up my mind.
Lucky you! Let's weigh up the pros and cons. What's the upside of the first one?
The salary is considerably higher. But the office is downtown, and the commute is far longer.
I see. And what about the second offer?
It's slightly less money, but I can work from home three days a week. It's by far the most flexible.
So the trade-off is money for time. Is the salary as important as your free time?
Not nearly as important. The only real drawback is that it's a much smaller company.
Then, on balance, I'd go for the second one. It sounds far more like you.

When people compare two options, they often look at one thing only, usually the price. But the cheapest option is not always the best one. Here is a simple method. First, write down what really matters to you, maybe three or four things. Then compare the options on each one, and be precise. Don't just say, this one is better. Say, this one is slightly cheaper, but the other one is far more comfortable. A small difference and a big difference are not the same thing, so use the right words. Finally, look at the drawbacks. Every option has a trade-off. The question is not, which option is perfect? The question is, which drawback can I live with? On balance, that question makes most decisions much easier.

Welcome back to Weekend Trips. This week, many of you asked me the same question: Ilhabela or Campos do Jordao? Here is my honest comparison. If you love the beach, Ilhabela is by far the better choice. The water is warm, and the island is gorgeous. Campos do Jordao is up in the mountains, and in winter it's considerably colder, so bring a good jacket. What about the price? Campos is not nearly as affordable as people think. In July, hotels there can cost twice as much. Ilhabela is slightly cheaper, but the ferry can take hours on a holiday weekend. That's its main drawback. So, on balance? In summer, go for Ilhabela. In winter, go for Campos, and book early.

First, I write down the two options. Then I list the pros and cons of each one. After that, I ask which drawback I can live with. Next, I compare them: this one is slightly cheaper, but that one is far closer. In the end, I go for the one that wins on balance.
